notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

I tried to open six pages at once: Enduring Word's Ezekiel 22 commentary, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit commentaries on BibleHub, Precept Austin's Ezekiel 22 page, and the NET Bible notes. They came back in a format my script didn't expect, and the tool stopped working before I could fix the script and read what they said. I can't search or open web pages any more this session.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no page content, writing verse notes now would mean making them up, so I haven't written any.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start by reading those same pages verse by verse. Then I'll look for:
- **Protestant differences:** each tradition's own teachers on the passages most likely to be read differently, especially v. 30 ("stand in the gap") and the priests in v. 26. Sources would include Spurgeon, Desiring God, Ligonier, Wesley's notes, the Gospel Coalition and the LCMS.
- **Other views:** Bible Odyssey and the NET notes for modern scholarship, and New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings.
- **Popular modern teaching:** "stand in the gap" as a basis for intercessory prayer, from GotQuestions and Pentecostal or charismatic sites.

I'll give a URL for every point and leave out anything I can't find.
